subject: math

objective.text: Use counters to make equal groups. Equal groups have the same number in each group.

explanations.title: Equal groups have the same number
explanations.text: Groups are equal when each group has the same number of counters. 3 groups with 2 counters in each are equal. A group of 4 and a group of 2 are unequal.

explanations.title: Say how many groups
explanations.text: To tell about equal groups, say: There are 4 groups of 2 counters. The first number is how many groups. The second number is how many in each group.

explanations.title: Many ways to make equal groups
explanations.text: You can make equal groups in more than one way. 12 counters make 2 groups of 6. They also make 3 groups of 4, 4 groups of 3, or 6 groups of 2.

explanations.title: Make unequal groups equal
explanations.text: Look at the group with the most counters and the group with the fewest. Move one counter from the most to the fewest. Keep checking until every group has the same number.

explanations.title: Split into 2 equal groups
explanations.text: To make 2 equal groups, share the counters into two rows. Or split them in half. A doubles fact can help you check.

examples.title: Equal or unequal: 6 counters
examples.text: 6 counters in 3 groups of 2 are equal. Every group has 2. Move them to 4 in one group and 2 in another. Now the groups are unequal.

examples.title: 8 counters
examples.text: 8 counters in groups of 2 make 4 groups. The same 8 counters in groups of 4 make 2 groups.

examples.title: 12 counters in equal groups
examples.text: 12 counters can make 2 groups of 6. They can make 3 groups of 4. They can make 4 groups of 3. They can make 6 groups of 2.

examples.title: 10 counters
examples.text: Set 2 counters aside from 12. Now 10 counters make 2 groups of 5. They also make 5 groups of 2.

examples.title: Make 3, 5 and 4 equal
examples.text: Three groups have 3, 5 and 4 counters. Move 1 counter from the group of 5 to the group of 3. Now there are 3 groups of 4.

examples.title: 12 counters in 2 equal groups
examples.text: Split 12 counters into 2 equal groups. Each group has 6. You can check with 6 plus 6 equals 12.
